Author: Saral Srivastava
Bench: Saral Srivastava
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 44302 of 2022
Applicant :- Ajay Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Hari Nath Chaubey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ghan Shyam Yadav

Hon'ble Saral Srivastava,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ghyan Shyam Yadav, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Ravi Prakash, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant-accused for release of his bail in Case Crime No.116 of 2021, under Sections 498A and 304B of I.P.C. & Section 3/4 of D.P. Act,
P.S. Sikandra, District Kanpur Dehat.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with some ulterior motive.
It is submitted that it is a case of false and malicious prosecution.

It is further submitted that demand of dowry as alleged in the prosecution story as well as in the statement of the first informant Sunil Kumar recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. is false and not supported by any material evidence on record.

It is further submitted that as per the report of handwriting expert, the handwriting of the deceased is matched Ajay Singh vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50074719/
1 with the handwriting of the suicide note.

entities.text: Ajay Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, it is submitted that the story set up by the prosecution is highly improbable.

It is further submitted that co-accused Smt. Anita Devi and Suneel Kumar have already been enlarged on bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application Nos.10092 of 2022 & 35809 of 2021 in same case crime number vide orders 23.03.2022 and 26.10.2021 respectively.

entities.text:
Criminal Misc.
Bail Application Nos.10092 of 2022 & 35809 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the applicant-accused has no criminal history and is languishing in jail since 30.07.2022.

Per contra learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the applicant alongwith his family members has committed cruelty with the deceased on account of which, she committed suicide, therefore, the applicant does not deserve any indulgence.
Further, learned counsel for the informant has produced certain receipts downloaded from the internet with regard to payment of money to the applicant-accused in the form of demand of dowry.
However, they could not dispute the fact that co-accused Smt. Anita Devi and Suneel Kumar have already been enlarged on bail by the coordinate Bench of this Court in the same case crime number.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, this Court cannot see the documents produced by the learned counsel for the informant at this stage, as they are not part of the case diary as per the statement of Sri Ravi Prakash, learned A.G.A for the State.

Further, considering the submission advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, nature of evidence and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court finds it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.

Accordingly, let applicant-Ajay Singh be released on bail in Case Crime No.116 of 2021, under Sections 498A and 304B of I.P.C. & Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Sikandra, District Kanpur Dehat on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as an abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation

,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
Ajay Singh vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50074719/
2 under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Ajay Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (v) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
It is further directed that the identity, status and residence proof of the sureties be verified by the authority concerned before they are accepted.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the trial court will be at liberty to cancel the bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
